title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Financial Interest in Litigation Outcome
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal agrees to represent a small business in a breach of contract dispute. Instead of billing hourly or taking a percentage of the winnings, the paralegal asks the client to assign 10% of the company's patent rights to the paralegal as payment for the lawsuit. Is this ethical?
options: Yes, it is an innovative alternative fee arrangement.
Yes, provided the patent rights are worth less than $35,000.
No, a paralegal must not acquire a personal financial interest in the subject matter of the litigation they are conducting, other than an authorized contingency fee.
No, paralegals cannot handle breach of contract claims.
questions.explain: Rule 3.06 strictly prohibits a practitioner from acquiring a proprietary or financial interest in the subject matter of the litigation or proceeding (such as the patents being disputed) to prevent a fundamental conflict of interest, except for taking a lawful contingency fee.
